Crist 636 (Cynewulf, Christ II; Exeter Book; Grein, Bibliothek I p. 166)

notes: The NP *priHóm h₁nómn̥ 'dear / own name' = Ved. priyáṃ nā́ma = OE frēo-nama. Scholarship: Scheller 1959 (Vedisch priyá- und die Wortsippe frei, freien, Freund, p. 68–76), reported by Schmitt 1967 §97 and §373 ('Laut für Laut entspricht dieser Wendung das altenglische freo nama') and West 2007 ch. 10 with n. 76 ('etymologically identical'). Caveat carried from Schmitt §97: a secure IE idiom, 'doch wohl noch lange nicht ein Bruchstück poetischer Phraseologie'; Scheller glosses *priHó- as 'eigen' (one's own), and the OE word means 'surname, cognomen' (Bede: freónama glosses cognomento), so 'dear' in the English is the Vedic sense; the inherited sense may be 'own, proper name'. Loci checked locally: RV 10.84.5c priyáṃ te nā́ma (acc. sg. n., the case of the line), RV 10.123.7d nā́ma janata priyā́ṇi (pl.), RV 7.56.10a priyā́ vo nā́ma (pl.), all in VedaWeb; OE Crist 636 freónoman cende in Grein's Bibliothek (Exeter Book, the only manuscript; Grein's apparatus has notes on 635 and 641 but none on 636, so freónoman is the manuscript reading, not an emendation). The OE word is univerbated (Bosworth–Toller hyphenate freó-nama): both members are cited as lemmas, frēo (< *frija- < *priH-o-, Kroonen s.v. *fri(j)a-) and nama (< *namon-, Kroonen). Formation: OE has a compound, Vedic a syntagm; the members are the same lexemes. The verb is interpolated from RV 10.123.7 janata (thematic present, injunctive middle 3sg per VedaWeb), here as the past middle of *ǵénh₁e-. Bosworth–Toller file Crist 636 cende under cennan I 'beget, create' (= Kroonen *kanjan- < *ǵonh₁-éye-, a causative), which would put *ǵenh₁- in both passages; but the homonym cennan 'declare, make known' (*kannjan-) fits 'named him bird' (Crist 636b) as well, and the formations differ (Ved. thematic middle, OE causative), so the verb is not claimed as secure. RV 10.84.5 has gṛṇīmasi 'we praise' and 7.56.10 huve 'I call' instead: no verb is shared by the three Vedic passages either.

Gm.locus: Vǫluspá 26 (FJ 1926; the refrain recurs in st. 32, 33, 38, 40, 50, 61, 62)

notes: The poet's address to the audience at the opening of a cosmogonic poem. Scholarship: Specht 1937 (ZVS 64: 1–3), reported in Schmitt 1967 §§48–49 and West 2007 ch. 2 with n. 61, compared the incipit of Vǫluspá 1 (Hljóðs biðk allar helgar kindir 'I ask a hearing of all the holy kindreds') with AV 20.127.1 idáṃ janā úpa śruta 'hear this, peoples' and AVŚ 1.32.1 idáṃ janāso vidatha 'know this, peoples', noting that both Vǫluspá and AVŚ 1.32 go on to cosmology; the etymological pairs Specht and Schmitt claim are hljóð : śru- (*ḱlew-) and kind : jána- (*ǵenh₁-). AV 20.127 is not in the local corpora (the DCS Śaunaka text ends at book 19), and in Vǫluspá 1 hljóð is the noun object of biðja, not a verb, so the 'hear' version is not used. This line rests instead on AVŚ 1.32.1, which is local, and the verb equation Ved. vidatha = ON vituð (ér) is my own addition, not Specht's: both are the 2pl of the perfect stem *wid- of *weyd- 'know' (Ved. perfect, DCS Tense=Past; ON preterite-present vita, cf. Goth. wituþ), so the head is shared at formation level (the endings are renewed on both sides: Ved. -tha for the expected vidá, Gmc *-ud). Mood: indicative in both (ON a question, 'do you know yet, or what?', the refrain the seeress addresses to her audience; Vedic indicative used as an exhortation: Whitney 'Now, ye people, take knowledge', checked in the Whitney translation shipped with the DCS). The head rests on one reading of vidatha: Whitney, Specht and the DCS annotation (2pl, Tense=Past, i.e. perfect) take it as the perfect of vid 'know'; a parse as a thematic aorist of vid 'find' (2pl vidáta) is formally possible but does not fit 'know this' before 'he will speak a great formulation'. Stitching, stated plainly: the ON verb stands only in the refrain stanzas (Vǫluspá 26 ff.), and the audience word kindir only in st. 1, where it is the accusative object of biðja; the refrain is addressed to that same audience, but no single ON stanza has both words. The vocative is root-level only: Ved. jána- (thematic *ǵónh₁o-, the lexeme realized here, glossed 'offspring') against ON kind (*ǵn̥h₁tí-, Lat. gēns); the builder's table maps them to different lexemes. The object 'it' (*id) follows Vedic idam and is interpolated (ON has enn 'yet' instead). The DCS lemma vid is ambiguous in the builder's table (it maps to the causative *woydéyeti), so the perfect-stem citation véda is added as a second lemma for vidatha. Avestan Y. 30.2a sraōtā gə̄ušāiš 'hear with your ears' (CAB) is support only for the Gathic call-to-hear opening (West ch. 2 also cites Y. 45.1, which is not in the CAB file). Graded weak by its author: the head is a single, common verb, and the frame is assembled from two stanzas of the ON poem. Eval grouping: Vǫluspá 1 is also a parallel locus in poetics-gifts-006 (other words: forn spjǫll, man) and a support ref in poetics-gifts-015 (Hljóðs biðk); group by source text.
